centre.name: Field Trip Health Ottawa
centre.address: 1 Centrepointe Dr, Unit 402, Ottawa, ON K2G 6E2, Canada

about_blocks.text: Field Trip Health Ottawa offers ketamine-assisted psychotherapy as an outpatient service. The clinic recently left its downtown suite on Sparks Street and now works from Unit 402 at 1 Centrepointe Drive in Nepean, a medical office building near Baseline Road and Woodroffe Avenue.
about_blocks.html: Field Trip Health Ottawa offers ketamine-assisted psychotherapy as an outpatient service. The clinic recently left its downtown suite on Sparks Street and now works from Unit 402 at 1 Centrepointe Drive in Nepean, a medical office building near Baseline Road and Woodroffe Avenue.

about_blocks.text: It treats adults with depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, chronic pain and substance use problems, mostly people for whom medication and counselling have not done enough. Appointments run on weekdays and you go home the same day. Staff speak mainly English, but services are also offered in French, which helps clients coming from Gatineau, Orleans, Rockland and Embrun.

Appointments run on weekdays and you go home the same day. Staff speak mainly English, but services are also offered in French, which helps clients coming from Gatineau, Orleans, Rockland and Embrun.

about_blocks.text: A free 15-minute discovery call comes first. After that you complete a questionnaire and see a nurse practitioner for a 50-minute medical consultation, which OHIP does not pay for. This is the gatekeeping step. The nurse practitioner looks at your health history and medications and may rule the treatment out for reasons such as pregnancy, a history of psychosis, uncontrolled hypertension or a recent serious head injury.

about_blocks.text: The standard plans have 6 or 9 dosing sessions, each about two and a half hours long. A nurse gives the medicine, usually as an intramuscular injection, and a therapist is with you from start to finish. You then meet that therapist for integration, where you work through the session and connect it to what you came in for.

about_blocks.text: Most of the Ottawa therapists are registered social workers or registered psychotherapists. One of them, Jason Taylor, is a doctoral-level psychotherapist who works mainly with depression, anxiety and OCD, and another, Amanda Laprade, specialises in substance use. The clinic also offers individual therapy and pain management, and lists neurofeedback as coming soon. It does not do MDMA or psilocybin therapy. The team also says it works closely with veterans, first responders, healthcare workers and Indigenous communities in the region.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Field Trip Health Ottawa

faqs.question: Where is Field Trip Health Ottawa now?

answer_blocks.text: The clinic has moved to 1 Centrepointe Drive, Unit 402, in the Centrepointe area of Nepean, Ottawa (K2G 6E2). It used to be at 350 Sparks Street downtown, and some directories and older directions still show that address. Parking at the new building costs extra, and you will need someone to drive you home after a dosing session.

faqs.question: Is Field Trip Health Ottawa a residential treatment centre?

answer_blocks.text: No. It is a weekday outpatient clinic, and you leave after each appointment. It has no beds and does not offer detox. People who need a live-in addiction program or withdrawal management should ask the team for other options or compare residential centres in Ottawa and Eastern Ontario.

faqs.question: Can I get treatment in French?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Staff at the Ottawa clinic mainly speak English, but the clinic says it also offers services in French and that its therapists are fluent in both languages. Mention your preference on the discovery call.

faqs.question: What conditions does the Ottawa clinic treat?

answer_blocks.text: Field Trip Health Ottawa uses ketamine-assisted psychotherapy mainly for depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, addiction and chronic pain. Its psychotherapists also work with grief, ADHD, bipolar disorder, eating disorders, complex PTSD and relationship concerns. The clinic describes the treatment as one possible option after other approaches, not a guaranteed fix.

faqs.question: How much does it cost, and does insurance help?

answer_blocks.text: The clinic does not publish its fees; the cost depends on how many sessions you have and how the medicine is given, and the team explains it on a free discovery call. The 50-minute nurse practitioner consult is not covered by OHIP. Psychotherapy or nursing benefits from an extended health plan often cover part of the cost, and third-party financing is available.

answer_blocks.text: Each dosing session at the Ottawa clinic takes about 2.5 hours, including preparation, the medicine and integration support. Most plans have 6 or 9 dosing sessions, followed by a review of whether more care would help.

faqs.question: Who is eligible, and do I need a referral?

answer_blocks.text: You do not need a referral to book the discovery call, though physicians and nurse practitioners can refer patients through Field Trip's referral form or Ocean eReferral. Eligibility is decided by a nurse practitioner. The treatment may not suit people who are pregnant, allergic to the medicine, have a history of schizophrenia or psychosis, uncontrolled hypertension or a recent severe head injury.

faqs.question: How do I prepare for a session?

answer_blocks.text: Avoid alcohol and recreational substances beforehand and eat a light meal rather than a heavy one. Arrange transport home, because you may feel drowsy and the clinic says you will not be able to drive.

faqs.question: Does the Ottawa clinic offer MDMA or psilocybin therapy?

answer_blocks.text: No. Only one psychedelic medicine can currently be prescribed for therapy in Canada, and that is the one the clinic uses, mainly by intramuscular injection. MDMA and psilocybin remain controlled substances that are not approved for routine clinical use.

faqs.question: Who operates Field Trip Health Ottawa?

answer_blocks.text: The Ottawa clinic is one of eight Canadian clinics run as Field Trip Health Canada. When the original Field Trip Health company restructured in 2023, the Canadian clinics were taken over by the Canadian Centre for Psychedelic Healing, while the US clinics went to a separate company. Use fieldtriphealth.ca to book in Ottawa.
